subject: Pricing follow-up: token volumes, budget, EU vs US costs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: lara.benson@nordichealth.eu, procurement@nordichealth.eu, mike@cloudintegrator.com
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-03T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Follow-up from Friday's discovery — token volumes, budget, region questions

Hi Lara / team,

Thanks again for the 30-minute discovery on Friday — helpful to see how NordicHealth plans to use summarization + embeddings for clinical notes search. I promised a quick follow-up with the unit-economics framing so your procurement and product teams can weigh options.

Top-line asks for us to confirm:
- Expected steady-state monthly token volumes (gen + embeds). If you prefer ranges, give low/likely/high.
- Target budget range for hosted inference (annual committed spend or monthly run-rate).
- Whether EU data residency is required for production, or a hybrid approach is acceptable for early PoC.

Quick notes from our side:
- We typically price on a $/1M tokens basis for generation-heavy apps; embeddings are priced per-embedding unit (we can map to tokens if helpful).
- EU-hosted execution typically carries a region premium (infrastructure + data residency controls) — ballpark +10–20% vs US hosted pricing depending on reserved capacity and KMS/HSM usage.

I've attached a starter pricing model (NDH_pricing_model_v1.xlsx) with slot-based scenarios and a draft DPA. If you can share simple volume numbers, I’ll drop a short comparison table (US vs EU monthly and annual $).

Next steps I propose:
1) You share low/likely/high monthly tokens by 2026-03-05.
2) We return a 1-page cost comparison and a recommended configuration (hosted vs dedicated) by 2026-03-06.
3) Procurement and legal loop in for DPA/contract redlines if numbers look good.

Thanks — happy to jump back on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: NDH_pricing_model_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 2 sheets)
From: Lara Benson <lara.benson@nordichealth.eu>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nordichealth.eu, mike@cloudintegrator.com
Date: 2026-03-04T10:34:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from Friday's discovery — token volumes, budget, region questions

Hi Marissa — thanks, useful email. Quick answers from our end:

Estimated steady-state volumes (production):
- Generation (summaries and assistants): 25M tokens / month (likely), range 15M–40M.
- Embeddings (semantic search + rerank): equivalent ~10M tokens / month (likely), range 5M–15M.
- Combined likely: 35M tokens / month; combined high: 55M; low: 20M.

Budget guidance (procurement):
- Target public-cloud hosted budget: EUR 40k–60k / month for inference at scale for year 1. That includes any infra premium for EU if required.
- Procurement would prefer a predictable $/1M token number to map to this range.

Residency:
- Production must meet EU data residency and we will require customer-managed KMS (managed HSM is ideal). PoC could run in US if necessary for speed, but plan for EU prod.

Timeframe: goal to have procurement conversations in April; decision target end of May.

Can you translate our 35M/month likely volume into (a) unit $/1M token target that fits the EUR 40k–60k budget and (b) delta vs US pricing if we require EU residency?

Thanks,
Lara
Lara Benson
Head of Product, NordicHealth
lara.benson@nordichealth.eu

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: lara.benson@nordichealth.eu
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, procurement@nordichealth.eu
Date: 2026-03-06T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from Friday's discovery — token volumes, budget, region questions

Lara — great context, thanks. Below is a concise cost translation and options so procurement can see the mapping. I also uploaded a slightly edited pricing tab to the attached workbook.

Assumptions we used:
- Volume baseline: 35M tokens / month (420M tokens / year).
- Baseline US-hosted unit: $125 per 1M tokens (generation-weighted blended rate we can hit with a reserved commitment).
- Embeddings priced as token-equivalent for this exercise (we can refine by vector unit later).
- EU region premium: +15% on hosted unit when EU residency + customer-managed KMS is required. For dedicated/private deployments, the premium can be amortized with reserved capacity (see options).

Simple math: (monthly)
- US-hosted: 35 * $125 = $4,375 / month (this is illustrative; note: $125/1M => 35 * 125)
- EU-hosted (baseline +15%): unit = $143.75 / 1M ; 35 * $143.75 = $5,031.25 / month
- Annualized: US ~ $52,500 ; EU ~ $60,375 (annual = monthly * 12)

To map to your EUR 40k–60k / month target, convert at 1 USD = 0.92 EUR (example today):
- US-hosted $4,375 => ~ EUR 4,025 / month (this is far below your target range; indicates you expect more committed features / reserved capacity + support + SSO/DPA costs in your budget)
- EU-hosted $5,031 => ~ EUR 4,628 / month

Interpretation and recommended next steps:
- Your stated EUR 40k–60k/month budget implies either much higher token volumes (x8–12 of the 35M number) or inclusion of additional services (dedicated GPUs, advanced SLAs, engineering integration, storage/retention, and enterprise support).
- If the 40k–60k range is a firm procurement band for inference alone, please confirm whether that includes onboarding/optional dedicated capacity. If yes, we can show a committed-reserved scenario with effective unit price closer to $80–100 / 1M tokens in exchange for a 12-month commit and reserved GPUs in EU. That would look like: 35M * $90 = $3,150 / month effective (but note committed reserved capacity typically requires minimums).

Options we can price for formal proposal:
A) Hosted (no reserved commit) — EU-hosted unit ~ $143.75 /1M; simple true-up billing.
B) Dedicated (reserved capacity) — 12-month commit; effective unit can fall to $80–100 /1M depending on commitment tier and workload profile. Additional monthly reserved fee applies for GPU capacity.
C) Private (VPC + on-prem controls) — higher add-on upfront; best for strict residency and HSM. Unit economics improve with larger commits.

Action items I can take this week:
- Populate the NDH_pricing_model_v1.xlsx with two commitment tiers (12m/24m) and show EU vs US monthly/annual numbers.
- Draft a short procurement note that calls out the extra items likely included in your EUR 40k–60k number (onboarding, SSO, HSM, logging retention).

Can you confirm whether the EUR 40k–60k band is intended for inference-only OR inference + reserved capacity + professional services?

If helpful I can also set a brief follow-up with Sean (solutions) and Dev (inference engineer) to align on dedicated sizing.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: updated NDH_pricing_model_v1.xlsx (pricing tab populated)

Date: 2026-03-09T13:45:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from Friday's discovery — token volumes, budget, region questions

Hi all — quick note from the integration side. Two practical items to flag that affect EU unit cost: 

1) Data residency + customer-managed KMS implies additional networking and key-rotation operations; for production we usually recommend Dedicated + VPC and an HSM-backed KMS. That configuration typically increases the platform line item but can reduce per-token costs if you commit to reserved GPU capacity.

2) Procurement cadence: expect ~45–75 days (legal + security review). If NordicHealth needs a firm number to put in an RFP, we can produce a committed-reserved estimate that targets an effective $/1M token in the $80–$95 range for EU with a 12–24 month commit, plus a monthly reserved capacity fee.

If you want, I can draft the technical notes for the SOW and add an appendix that lists the EU infra premium drivers (HSM, cross-region DR, additional logging retention).

—Mike
Mike Rao
Solutions Engineer, CloudIntegrator (partner)
Attachments referenced: none
